articles.summary: Federal cannabis reform in 2026 is gaining measurable momentum, but industry leaders caution that rescheduling and safe banking are not immediate solutions for operators. At IgniteIt’s New Jersey Spotlight panel, Nabis CEO Vince C. Ning joined capital markets and policy experts to break down what federal cannabis rescheduling, safe banking legislation, hemp regulation, and interstate commerce could realistically mean for licensed operators. While the potential shift from Schedule I to Schedule III could ease 280E tax burdens, panelists emphasized that regulatory clarity, IRS interpretation, and implementation timelines will determine real impact. Discussions also highlighted how federal cannabis policy is evolving from plant-based frameworks toward cannabinoid-centric regulation, signaling structural change across compliance, packaging, and interstate distribution. The takeaway: federal cannabis reform represents a long-term tailwind for the industry, not a short-term lifeline. For operators navigating compliance risk, capital constraints, and market volatility, disciplined fundamentals remain essential as Washington’s policy landscape continues to evolve.
articles.title: Federal Cannabis Reform in 2026: Why Industry Leaders Call It a Tailwind, Not a Lifeline

articles.summary: Nabis rebuilt its B2B cannabis marketplace on real-time data replication via Kafka, replacing batch-synced systems that couldn't keep pace with inventory changes across California and New York. The result: accurate reorders, faster search, and a multi-cart experience for retailers managing multiple licensed locations — all updating in milliseconds.
articles.title: From Fragmented to Real-Time: Rebuilding a Marketplace That Moves at the Speed of Demand

articles.summary: In a California cannabis market defined by premium positioning and lifestyle branding, Pacific Stone took a different path. The family-owned greenhouse brand — founded in 2015 and based in Carpinteria, California — built its reputation on quality, consistency, and accessible pricing. Today, Pacific Stone is one of the most consistently recommended affordable cannabis brands in California, with a catalog spanning pre-roll tins, hemp-wrapped blunts, and large-format flower that has made it a first recommendation at dispensaries across the state.
articles.title: Inside Pacific Stone: Decade of California Cannabis from a Family-Owned Carpinteria Greenhouse
